description: Bridges a decided rule dispute (seeds/rule_dispute_escalation.json) to a self-conscious-emotion appraisal (seeds/self_conscious_emotions.json) for the claim-holder who was wrong, WITHOUT editing either seed -- strictly additive. The dispute's escalate/defuse outcome IS the correction style (Tangney & Dearing 2002: hostile/confrontational vs calm), which sets attribution_locus (global_self vs specific_act) and, identically, each carried-over witness's judgment. standard_met is unconditionally 0.0 -- a dispute existing at all means the claim-holder was wrong. This bridge structurally never produces attribution_locus=circumstance, so it never produces embarrassment -- a genuine rules dispute is an attributable epistemic error, not a circumstantial mishap (PREREG Sec1's registered scope boundary, prediction 3). Zero new Rust Terms -- Eq/And/IfThenElse/Count/Neighbours/Attr/Var/Lit all pre-existed; add_node/add_edge rule effects mirror seeds/gap_awareness.json's own mint-on-decision idiom exactly. See RULE_DISPUTE_SELF_CONSCIOUS_BRIDGE_PREREG.md / _RESULTS.md.

concepts.name: rule_dispute_self_conscious_bridge
concepts.definition: A rules dispute's escalate/defuse outcome IS a correction style (hostile/confrontational vs calm), which mechanically determines the self-conscious emotion the disputant who was wrong experiences -- shame from an escalated confrontation, guilt from a defused correction -- via the same attribution-locus mechanism the self-conscious-emotions rung already established, never a bespoke third decision.
concepts.why: The user asked to wire the self-conscious-emotions mechanism live off the rule-dispute escalation outcome, the follow-on both prior RESULTS docs named. RULE_DISPUTE_SELF_CONSCIOUS_BRIDGE_PREREG.md.

rules.name: bridge_dispute_to_self_conscious_context
rules.comment: PREREG Sec1: a decided RuleDisputeSignal mints a SelfConsciousContext for the claim-holder -- standard_met=0.0 unconditionally (the dispute's own premise is that this party was wrong about the rule, RULE_DISPUTE_ESCALATION_PREREG.md Sec2). attribution_locus and witness_judgment are both derived from the SAME outcome-keyed mapping (Tangney & Dearing 2002: a hostile/confrontational correction (escalate) reads as global-self attribution; a calm one (defuse) reads as specific-act) -- not two independent decisions. Guarded by a bridged_to dedup edge so re-running run_rules() does not double-mint (PREREG prediction 5).

rules.name: bridge_dispute_witness_to_self_conscious_witness
rules.comment: PREREG Sec1/prediction 4: each WitnessPresence already on the dispute's DisputeContext mints a corresponding WitnessBelief on the bridged SelfConsciousContext, judgment taken from the SAME witness_judgment Rule 1 already derived (not re-derived here) -- an escalated (public, confrontational) dispute reads to onlookers as a clear violation; a defused one does not. Guarded by a mirrored_as dedup edge per witness (PREREG prediction 5).
